method: Found while reading every cell of every stored NASA PSI combustion table into the Fire Test Atlas, plus cross-checks: gas fractions that should sum to 1, oxygen before and after a burn, identical rows, repeated identifiers and the same material across tables. Nothing in NASA's files is changed; each issue says how EMBER handles it. The tables were not compared with their source papers.

issues.title: Value outside physical limits
issues.detail: The value is outside physical limits for its quantity, so it is not used (the raw cell is kept).
issues.handling: Not used as a number; the raw cell is kept.

issues.title: Fuel label counts up row by row (spreadsheet fill-down)
issues.detail: The fuel label counts up row by row ("40% CH5", "CH6"…, or "N3", "N4"…), a spreadsheet fill-down; the real gas is not stated.
issues.handling: No fuel name is assigned; the label is kept as written.

issues.title: Fuel label counts up row by row (spreadsheet fill-down)
issues.detail: The fuel label counts up row by row ("40% CH5", "CH6"…, or "N3", "N4"…), a spreadsheet fill-down; the real gas is not stated.
issues.handling: No fuel name is assigned; the label is kept as written.

issues.title: Final oxygen that a glovebox burn cannot produce
issues.detail: Final O₂ differs from initial O₂ by more than 5 points in one burn, which a glovebox burn cannot do; likely a transcription slip.
issues.handling: The row is kept but left out of the carbon-monoxide finding (F4).

issues.title: Typo in a material label
issues.detail: The label has a typo (e.g. "blac", "2ide", "parrafin"); matched with its evident meaning.
issues.handling: Matched with its evident meaning; the label is kept as written.

issues.title: Typo in a material label
issues.detail: The label has a typo (e.g. "blac", "2ide", "parrafin"); matched with its evident meaning.
issues.handling: Matched with its evident meaning; the label is kept as written.

issues.title: Gas mole fractions do not add up to 1
issues.detail: The oxygen, nitrogen and added-gas fractions of the ambient gas should sum to 1. On these rows they do not, so one fraction is mistyped or a gas is missing from the table.
issues.handling: Values are kept as written; the rows stay in the findings because oxygen is the only fraction they use.

issues.title: Column header lost its subscripts
issues.detail: NASA's header lost its subscripts ("O" is O₂, "CO" is CO₂ in FLEX); read with that meaning.
issues.handling: Read with the evident meaning (O is O₂, CO is CO₂, N is N₂ in FLEX's composition columns).

issues.title: Header unit does not fit the quantity
issues.detail: The header's unit (mm) does not fit a burning rate; values are kept in the unit as stated.
issues.handling: Values are kept in the unit as stated and not used in any finding.

issues.title: Test identifier used twice
issues.detail: Each FLEX run has its own identifier, but this one appears on two rows with different results.
issues.handling: EMBER identifies rows by table and row number, never by NASA's identifier, so both rows are kept apart.

issues.title: Value outside physical limits
issues.detail: The value is outside physical limits for its quantity, so it is not used (the raw cell is kept).
issues.handling: Not used as a number; the raw cell is kept.

issues.title: Same fabric, three different thicknesses
issues.detail: Saffire-I, II and III all burned SIBAL cotton-fiberglass fabric, but its thickness is written 0.37 under a cm header, "037 mm" and ".33 cm". A fabric sheet is a fraction of a millimetre thick, so the cm values look like unit slips.
issues.handling: No thickness is used for SIBAL in any finding; each cell is kept as written.

issues.title: Sample length and width look swapped
issues.detail: Length and width are the reverse of the Saffire-III table for the same 94 × 40.6 cm sheet format.
issues.handling: Kept as written and flagged; not used in any finding.

issues.title: Typo in a material label
issues.detail: The label has a typo (e.g. "blac", "2ide", "parrafin"); matched with its evident meaning.
issues.handling: Matched with its evident meaning; the label is kept as written.

issues.title: Column header lost the µ in µ-g
issues.detail: NASA's header lost the µ ("?-g" is µ-g); read with that meaning.
issues.handling: Read as µ-g (microgravity).

issues.title: Number missing its decimal point
issues.detail: A number written with a leading zero and no decimal point (e.g. "037 mm"), so its magnitude is ambiguous; not used.
issues.handling: Not used: the magnitude is ambiguous. The raw cell is kept.

issues.title: Typo in a column header
issues.detail: NASA's header has a typo ("Samle Thickness"); read with its evident meaning.
issues.handling: Read with its evident meaning.

issues.title: Spreadsheet error left in a cell
issues.detail: The cell holds a spreadsheet error (e.g. "#DIV/0!").
issues.handling: Not used.

issues.title: Reading off the instrument's scale
issues.detail: The reading was off the instrument's scale (">500", "OR", "over"); no number is used.
issues.handling: No number is used; counted separately in F4.

issues.title: Material cell blank on a test row
issues.detail: The material cell is blank on a row with test data; EMBER does not fill it in.
issues.handling: Not filled in; the test is reported as "not stated in NASA's table".

issues.title: Flow marked RAMPED, so the run has no single value
issues.detail: NASA marks the flow as RAMPED, so the run has no single fuel fraction or flow.
issues.handling: No number is used for the ramped columns.

issues.title: Flow marked RAMPED, so the run has no single value
issues.detail: NASA marks the flow as RAMPED, so the run has no single fuel fraction or flow.
issues.handling: No number is used for the ramped columns.

issues.title: Text in a numeric column
issues.detail: The cell holds text, not a number; kept as written.
issues.handling: Kept as text; no number is used.

issues.title: Lines that are not tests inside the test table
issues.detail: Footnotes, flow-visualisation lines, cleaning runs, continuation lines or empty lines sit among the test rows, so a row count overstates the number of tests.
issues.handling: Marked as asides with the reason, and left out of every count of tests.

issues.title: Rows identical in every column
issues.detail: Two or more rows have the same value in every column the table records. They may be genuine repeat runs that the table cannot tell apart, or duplicated lines.
issues.handling: Every row is kept as its own test; findings that count tests say so.

issues.title: Negative instrument reading
issues.detail: A negative instrument reading (e.g. CO of -1 ppm); kept as written.
issues.handling: Kept as written (air rates below zero are not used as a flow).

issues.title: Oxygen higher after the burn than before
issues.detail: A burn uses up oxygen, so the final reading should not be above the initial one. These rows rise by about 0.1 point, which is within what a sensor can drift; they may also record a top-up of the glovebox air.
issues.handling: Kept as written.
